speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a longstanding pruritic rash with numbness and tingling on your palms. To understand the underlying cause, are you experiencing joint pain, fatigue, or any other systemic symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details. Given your occupation on a rice farm and with livestock, have you experienced any joint swelling, morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes, or small, firm lumps under your skin?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, RF, Anti-CCP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_close_up_of_rash, Ultrasound_of_synovium.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal inflammatory markers and negative autoimmune serologies rule out common rheumatologic causes like rheumatoid arthritis. Given your occupation on a rice farm and the specific location of your symptoms, have you noticed any small, firm, painless lumps under the skin on your hands or wrists, and do you experience dry, waxy-looking skin?

REQUEST TEST: ANA, Anti-SSA, Anti-SSB.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_close_up_of_rash, Ultrasound_of_synovium.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your inflammatory markers and autoimmune tests are normal, I need to rule out an infectious cause given your farm exposure. Have you had any contact with wild animals, and do you recall any insect bites or mosquito exposure in the past year?

REQUEST TEST: ELISA for Leishmania, Serology for Chagas (Trypanosoma cruzi).
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_close_up_of_rash, Ultrasound_of_synovium.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative infectious workup and lack of systemic symptoms make a parasitic etiology less likely. Given the specific combination of pruritic rash, paresthesias on the palms, and your work on a rice farm, have you noticed any small, firm, painless subcutaneous nodules on your hands or feet, or a rash that looks like scattered red spots resembling seeds?

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_of_skin_nodule, ANA.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy_of_skin_nodule: Findings show a granulomatous infiltrate with acid-fast bacilli consistent with leprosy. ANA: Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Leprosy (Hansen's Disease).

The skin biopsy confirms granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli, which is pathognomonic for leprosy, explaining your rash, palm numbness, and history of farm exposure.
